objectives: Students will analyze connections between socioemotional wellbeing and professional performance.
Students will identify evidence-based strategies to sustain wellness and prevent burnout.
Students will apply reflective and restorative practices to enhance self-awareness and emotional regulation.
Students will evaluate systemic and cultural influences on practitioner wellbeing.
Students will create a personalized wellness framework to support long-term personal and professional balance.
topics: The Practitioner as a Person: overview of course; defining socioemotional wellness and wholeness; exploring practitioner
The Science of Wellbeing: foundations of emotional intelligence, stress physiology, and the mind-body connection.
Systems of Care and the Cost of Caring: understanding burnout, compassion fatigue, and vicarious trauma.
Mindfulness and Self-Regulation Practices: exploration of mindfulness, breathwork, and embodied awareness as resilience
Boundaries and Balance: establishing professional boundaries and navigating emotional labor.
Cultural Contexts of Wellness: examining how race, gender, and culture shape wellness experiences and expectations.
Trauma-Informed and Healing-Centered Practice: applying trauma-informed principles to sustain personal and community wel
Midterm Reflection and Integration: guided reflection; developing insights from personal practice logs and class discuss
The Role of Community and Connection: building professional support systems and collective care networks.
The Spiritual Dimension of Wholeness: exploring purpose, meaning-making, and alignment in professional life.
Environmental and Organizational Wellness: analyzing workplace cultures and institutional supports for wellbeing.
Creative and Restorative Practices: engaging art, movement, and creativity as wellness modalities.
Practicing with Wellness in Mind: integrating socioemotional wellness into career practices.
Designing a Personal Wellness Framework: developing individualized and context-specific wellness plans.

objectives: Students will be able to investigate theories and practices of inquiry-based pedagogies.
Students will be able to read and examine theories of writing and writing pedagogies.
Students will be able to explore how writing and inquiry can facilitate teacher leadership.
Students will be able to study theories and practices of equity in education.
Students will be able to design classroom spaces and practices for inquiry and for writing.
Students will be able to form inquiry/writing groups for burning questions and responsive feedback.
Students will be able to write for different purposes and audiences.
Students will be able to design an inquiry project focused on the intersection of writing, teaching, and equity in global and local spaces that enable teacher leadership.
topics: Teacher as leader/designer of inquiry-based pedagogies 2.
Teacher as leader of equity practices and projects 3.
Teacher as writer and researcher: developing habitual practices of writing and inquiry in the service of leadership 4.
The enabling conditions of space and place in teaching, writing, inquiry, and leadership 5.
What researchers say about writing and teaching writing 6.
Whole group, small group, and individual writing instruction 7.
Designing an inquiry project 8.
Engaging with an inquiry group throughout the course 9.
Crafting pedagogies and lessons learned from the inquiry through writing and presentations 10.
Teacher as collaborative leader 11.
Facilitating writing groups 12.
Providing writing feedback 13.
Accepting and incorporating writing feedback 14.
Presenting the findings of inquiry projects to different audiences 15.
